fingerprints.story: The wind off the North Sea did not merely blow; it screamed, a constant, jagged shriek that battered the granite walls of the Blackwood Point Lighthouse. Inside the lantern room, however, the air was still, thick with the scent of old brass, whale oil, and the metallic tang of ozone. Elias Thorne, a man whose skin had weathered into the texture of driftwood, sat hunched over his workbench. Before him lay the broken heart
